NEW PATIENT — establishing care
52F, teaches math at the high school. Transferring from her previous primary care office; release signed for records today.

HTN: on lisinopril 20 and HCTZ 12.5 for years. Rarely checks at home. No headache, chest pain or swelling.
T2DM: metformin 1000 BID, takes it with breakfast and dinner, no GI upset. No lows. Last eye exam she thinks was two summers ago.
ADPKD: father had polycystic kidneys. Hers was found on ultrasound in 2016. Prior office checked kidney function yearly. No flank pain, no blood in the urine she has noticed.
DVT 2021: leg clot, three months of a blood thinner, finished, nothing since.
Lichen sclerosus (vulvar): diagnosed 2018 by her gynecologist, uses clobetasol ointment when it flares, sees gyn yearly.

PSH: none.
Meds: lisinopril 20 mg daily, HCTZ 12.5 mg daily, metformin 1000 mg BID, clobetasol 0.05% oint BID prn.
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: father ADPKD, ruptured brain aneurysm, HTN. Mother breast cancer at 62, T2DM. Sister HTN.
SH: lives with her partner; grown son. Smoked about 10 pack-years, quit in 2015. Wine once or twice a week. No drugs.

ROS: negative except as above.
Exam: pleasant, no distress. Vitals in flowsheet; BP fine on her two meds.
HEENT clear. Neck supple, thyroid normal size. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no masses felt. No edema. Feet: skin intact, monofilament normal both feet, DP pulses 2+.

A/P
1. HTN — at goal. Continue lisinopril/HCTZ. CMP today.
2. T2DM — A1c and urine microalbumin today. Needs a dilated eye exam this year; list of local optometrists given. Foot exam normal.
3. ADPKD — baseline creatinine today, will trend with each visit.
4. Hx DVT — off anticoagulation, no symptoms.
5. Vulvar lichen sclerosus — continue clobetasol as needed, keep yearly gyn visits.
6. Health maintenance — HCV and HIV screening once (today). Colonoscopy 2020 per pt, confirm with records. Mammogram due in March. Flu and COVID shots in October. Pneumococcal vaccine at next visit given diabetes. PHQ-2 negative.

RTC 3 months.

OUTSIDE GASTROENTEROLOGY — consultation letter
Date of visit: 05/16/2023
Re: Valerie Slattery, DOB 02/09/1970

Reason for referral: heartburn and regurgitation.

Ms. Slattery is a 53-year-old teacher with about six months of on-and-off heartburn and regurgitation, mostly after meals and clearly worse when she lies flat. Over-the-counter antacids have not helped. She denies dysphagia, odynophagia, vomiting, melena or weight loss.

PMH: hypertension, type 2 diabetes, ADPKD, DVT in 2021 (treated), vulvar lichen sclerosus. No prior surgery.
Medications: lisinopril 20 mg daily, hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg daily, metformin 1000 mg twice daily, clobetasol ointment as needed.
Allergies: no known drug allergies.
Social: former smoker (quit 2015), wine 1-2 glasses weekly.

Exam: vital signs normal. Abdomen soft, nontender, no organomegaly or masses.

Chest radiograph obtained today shows a retrocardiac opacity with an air-fluid level, which in this setting most likely represents a hiatal hernia.

Impression: gastroesophageal reflux disease, probable hiatal hernia.
Plan:
1. Omeprazole 20 mg daily, 30 minutes before breakfast.
2. Upper endoscopy to evaluate the hernia and the esophageal mucosa; our office will schedule.
3. Reflux precautions reviewed.

Thank you for involving us in her care.
Gastroenterology

GYNECOLOGY OFFICE NOTE (outside practice), copy to primary care
Visit: 11/01/2023
Patient: Valerie Slattery, 53

Seen sooner than her routine visit at the request of her PCP. Known vulvar lichen sclerosus, diagnosed here five years ago, managed with intermittent topical steroid. For about six months she has had itching and discomfort that keep getting worse; adding over-the-counter hydrocortisone did nothing.

Other history: hypertension, type 2 diabetes, polycystic kidney disease, DVT 2021, reflux with a hiatal hernia.
Meds: lisinopril, hydrochlorothiazide, metformin, omeprazole, clobetasol ointment.
Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: vulva with several pale, thinned, atrophic-appearing patches typical of her lichen sclerosus. On the left labium majus there is a new firm white plaque measuring about 1 cm. No inguinal lymph nodes palpable on either side. Vagina and cervix normal; bimanual exam unremarkable.

Procedure: after consent and local lidocaine, 4 mm punch biopsy of the left labial plaque. Hemostasis with silver nitrate. Tolerated well.

Assessment: lichen sclerosus with a new firm plaque, biopsied to exclude neoplasia.
Plan: pathology in about a week, will call her. Continue clobetasol to the surrounding skin. Sitz baths for comfort.
Gynecology

GYNECOLOGIC ONCOLOGY — NEW PATIENT CONSULTATION
Date of service: 11/21/2023
Patient: Valerie Slattery   DOB: 02/09/1970
Referred by her gynecologist; copy to primary care.

53-year-old with longstanding vulvar lichen sclerosus and a 1 cm firm plaque of the left labium majus. Punch biopsy: invasive keratinizing squamous cell carcinoma, depth of invasion 0.8 mm.

PMH: HTN, T2DM, ADPKD, DVT 2021, GERD with hiatal hernia, vulvar lichen sclerosus. PSH: none. Medications: lisinopril, HCTZ, metformin, omeprazole, clobetasol. Allergies: NKDA. Former smoker.

Exam: well-appearing. Left labium majus with a healing biopsy site within a firm white plaque, roughly 1 cm, well away from the clitoris, urethra and anus. Background pallor and atrophy of lichen sclerosus. No palpable groin nodes bilaterally.

Impression: clinically early vulvar SCC, lesion about 1 cm with superficial invasion on biopsy.
Plan: radical local excision of the left labial lesion with 1 cm margins. If final depth of invasion is 1 mm or less, no groin node evaluation is needed. Risks reviewed, consent signed. Surgery scheduled 12/05.
Afterward she will need lifelong surveillance because of the lichen sclerosus; we will see her every 6 months, alternating with her gynecologist after the first two years.
Gynecologic Oncology

reports.text: Specimen: vulva, left labium majus, radical local excision, oriented. Invasive keratinizing squamous cell carcinoma, 1.1 cm in greatest dimension, depth of invasion 0.8 mm. No lymphovascular invasion. All margins negative; closest margin 9 mm (medial). Background lichen sclerosus.
reports.conclusion: Invasive squamous cell carcinoma of the left labium majus, 1.1 cm, depth of invasion 0.8 mm, margins negative (closest 9 mm), no lymphovascular invasion. FIGO stage IA.

documents.title: Radical local excision, left vulva
documents.author: gynecologic oncology
documents.body:
OPERATIVE SUMMARY — outside gynecologic oncology
Date: 12/05/2023
Procedure: radical local excision, left labium majus, with layered closure.
Anesthesia: general. Allergies: NKDA. EBL minimal. No complications. Discharged home the same day.

Final pathology (12/08): invasive keratinizing SCC, 1.1 cm, depth of invasion 0.8 mm, no LVI, margins negative with the closest at 9 mm. FIGO stage IA.

Plan: no groin node surgery and no adjuvant treatment needed. Post-op check in 2 weeks. Surveillance exams every 6 months. She should keep using clobetasol to the remaining lichen sclerosus, which lowers the chance of a new lesion. Any new lump, sore or bleeding should be seen promptly.
Gynecologic Oncology

MEDICAL ONCOLOGY — treatment visit, cycle 1 day 1
Date: 05/07/2026
Patient: Valerie Slattery, 56

Here to begin adjuvant chemotherapy for recently diagnosed left breast IDC, pT2 N0, stage IIA, grade 2, ER+/PR+/HER2-, recurrence score 31. Lumpectomy with SLNB 4/16 (3 weeks ago); right chest port placed 4/30 (1 week ago).
Other history: HFrEF (LVEF 35%, nonischemic), left atrial myxoma excised 5/2025, ruptured right MCA aneurysm coiled 11/2025, PE 11/2024 (completed anticoagulation), DVT 2021, right frontal meningioma resected 5/2024, stage IA vulvar SCC 12/2023, hypertension, type 2 diabetes, ADPKD, GERD.
Medications: furosemide 40 mg daily, potassium chloride 20 mEq daily, lisinopril 20 mg daily, metformin 1000 mg BID, omeprazole 20 mg daily, clobetasol ointment as needed.
Allergies: NKDA.

Vitals within normal limits. Exam unremarkable apart from healing lumpectomy, axillary and port incisions without erythema.
Labs: hemoglobin 13.2, WBC 7.8, platelets 250, AST/ALT 20/22, bilirubin 0.8; renal function at her baseline.

Plan:
- Docetaxel 75 mg/m2 and cyclophosphamide 600 mg/m2 IV every 21 days x 4 cycles, given today. No anthracycline because of her ejection fraction.
- Pegfilgrastim on-body injector applied today.
- Dexamethasone 8 mg twice daily for 3 days starting the day before each docetaxel dose (taken yesterday), for fluid retention and reactions. Expect higher sugars on those days.
- Ondansetron 8 mg every 8 hours as needed for nausea.
- Next cycle 5/28. Radiation oncology after chemotherapy, then endocrine therapy.

documents.title: Nausea and vomiting after cycle 1
documents.author: oncology RN
documents.body:
ONCOLOGY NURSE TELEPHONE NOTE (copy to PCP)
Ms. Slattery called this morning. Nausea started the day after cycle 1 and she vomited several times on days 2 through 4, worst on Saturday. Ondansetron helped for a few hours at a time. documents.title: RE: Steroids and my sugar
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Glad this cycle is going better. Dexamethasone does raise blood sugar for a day or two around each treatment, and it settles once the doses are done.
